The matrix assessment procedure involved the assignment of two numbers ranging from 1 to 10 for each interaction. One number indicates the presumed magnitude of the possible impact, where 10 represents the greatest magnitude and 1, the least. The second number indicates the importance of the possible impact; again, 10 represents the greatest magnitude and 1, the least. We have simplified the matrix in this Impact Statement by assigning a single value constituting an average of both the magnitude and importance of the possible impacts. Details of our choice of numbers are specifically discussed for each area of possible environmental impact in the matrix. Each aspect of influence of this project, relevant to the environments of the Ross Ice Shelf, has been assessed accordingly and all are listed summarily in Table 2; particular attention is given to them in the following descriptions:
1. <u>Airstrip</u>. The use of LC-130 ski-equipped airplanes will lead to compaction of the snow and firn, and temporary minor changes in local atmospheric quality and microclimate due to turbo-jet engine exhaust. It is recognized that the frequency of use will have an influence in the scale of the effects resulting from aircraft operations. However, the anticipated operations should not have an impact of any significance.
